description: relay_queue.rs seeds the LazyLock<AtomicU64> counter from SystemTime epoch nanoseconds, so IDs are globally unique across restarts and sort chronologically. queue.rs uses a plain AtomicU64 starting at 0, so IDs restart from zero on every process restart and can collide with IDs from a previous run if the queue directory is not empty. Both modules call their function unique_id(). The inconsistency is a latent correctness bug: if the NNTP queue ever needs replay-safe IDs (e.g. for crash recovery), the zero-based counter will produce collisions. Fix: use the same epoch-seeded LazyLock pattern in queue.rs, or extract a shared unique_id() to a common module.
title: smtp: unique_id() inconsistency between relay_queue and queue
